"וישלח יעקב מלאכים". אמר רבי אבא, וכי אמאי אתער איהו לגביה דעשו, וטב הוה ליה לאשתוקי מניה, אלא אמר יעקב, ידענא דעשו חייש ליה ליקרא דאבא, ולעלם לא ארגיז קמיה, והא ידענא הואיל ואבא קיים לא מסתפינא מניה, אבל השתא דאבא קאים בעינא לאתפייס עמיה, מיד וישלח יעקב מלאכים לפניו. 


"וישלח יעקב מלאכים". רבי שמעון פתח ואמר, (משלי יב ט) "טוב נקלה ועבד לו, ממתכבד וחסר לחם". האי קרא על יצר


הרע אתמר, בגין דאיהו מקטרגא תדיר לגבי בני נשא, ויצר הרע איהו ארים לביה ורעותיה דבר נש בגאותא, ואזיל אבתריה מסלסל שעריה וברישיה, עד דאיהו אתגאי עליה ומשיך ליה לגיהנם, אבל טוב נקלה ההוא דלא אזיל אבתריה דיצר הרע, ולא אתגאי כלל, ומאיך רוחיה ולביה ורעותיה לגבי קב"ה, וכדין ההוא יצר הרע מתהפך לעבד לו, דלא יכיל לשלטאה עלוי, וההוא בר נש שליט עלוי, כמה דאת אמר (בראשית ד ז) ואתה תמשל בו.     "ממתכבד"-- כמה דאמרן דאיהו אוקיר גרמיה מסלסל בשעריה אתגאי ברוחיה, ואיהו חסר לחם, חסר מהימנותא, כמה דאת אמר (ויקרא כא כב) לחם אלהי"ו וגו', (ויקרא כא ו) לחם אלהיהם הם מקריבים וגו'. 


דבר אחר: "טוב נקלה (ועבד לו)" -- דא יעקב, דמאיך רוחיה לגביה דעשו, בגין דלבתר ליהוי עבד לו וישלוט עלוי, ויתקיים ביה (בראשית כז כט) יעבדוך עמים וישתחוו לך לאומים וגו', ועדיין לא הוה זמניה כלל, אלא בגין דסליק ליה יעקב לבתר יומיא, ועל דא הוה מיד נקלה, ולבתר ההוא דאיהו מתכבד יהא עבד לו, ההוא דאיהו חסר לחם, יהא עבדא לההוא דיהבו ליה רוב דגן ותירוש. 


תא חזי, על דא בגין דידע יעקב דאצטריך ליה השתא אתהפך ליה נקלה, ויותר חכמה ועקימו עבד בדא, מכל מה דעבד לגביה דעשו, דאילו הוה ידע עשו חכמה דא, יקטיל ליה לגרמיה ולא ייתי לדא, אבל כלא עבד בחכמתא, ועליה אמרה חנה (שמואל א ב י) יהו"ה יחתו מריביו וגו', ויתן עז למלכו וגו':
english:
“Ya'akoav sent angels.” Rabbi Abbuh said: Why did he stir himself to approach Aisuv? It would have been better for him to remain silent toward him! Rather, Ya'akoav said: “I know that Aisuv is concerned for Father's honor, and he never gives vent to anger in his presence. I know that as long as Father is alive, I am not afraid of him. But now, while Father is alive, I want to be reconciled with him.” Immediately, “Ya'akoav sent angels before him.”

“Ya'akoav sent angels.” Rabbi Shimon opened and said: “Better one lightly esteemed who has a servant than one who honors himself but lacks bread” (Mishlay 12:9). This verse was said concerning the evil inclination, because it is constantly an accuser against human beings. The evil inclination raises a person's heart and will in pride, and he follows after it, arranging his hair and [the hair] on his head, until it grows overbearing toward him and draws him to Gaihinum. But “better one lightly esteemed”: that is the person who does not follow the evil inclination and does not grow proud at all, but lowers his spirit, heart and will before the Holy One, blessed be He. Then that evil inclination becomes his servant: it cannot rule over him, and that person rules over it, as you say, “And you shall rule over it” (Biraishis 4:7). “Than one who honors himself”—as we have said: he honors himself, arranges his hair and grows proud in his spirit. He “lacks bread”: he lacks faith, as you say, “The bread of his God,” and so forth (Va'yeekruh 21:22), and, “The bread of their God they offer,” and so forth (Va'yeekruh 21:6).

Another interpretation: “Better one lightly esteemed (who has a servant)”—this is Ya'akoav, who lowered his spirit before Aisuv so that afterward [Aisuv] would be his servant and he would rule over him, and there would be fulfilled in him: “Peoples shall serve you, and nations bow down to you,” and so forth (Biraishis 27:29). His time had not yet come at all; rather, Ya'akoav deferred it to the end of days. Therefore he was, for the present, lightly esteemed; afterward, the one who honors himself would be his servant. The one who lacks bread would be a servant to the one to whom an abundance of grain and new wine had been given.

Come and see: therefore, because Ya'akoav knew that he needed this now, he made himself lightly esteemed before him. In this he acted with more wisdom and cunning than in everything he had done toward Aisuv. Had Aisuv known this wisdom, he would have killed himself rather than come to this. But he [Ya'akoav] did everything with wisdom. Of him Channuh said: “Hashem—His adversaries shall be shattered,” and so forth, “and He will give strength to His king,” and so forth (I Samuel 2:10).

notes.he: העד הדיגיטלי כאן אינו מנוקד ושונה מן העד היומי המנוקד בכתיב, בצורות שמות הקודש, בקיצורים ובנוסחאות מוסגרות. ציוני הפסוקים, גבולות הציטוטים וסימני הסיום הם תלויי נוסח; אין הכרח שיהיו זהים בדפוס היומי.
notes.en: The digital witness here is unpointed and differs from the pointed daily witness in spelling, Divine-Name forms, abbreviations and parenthetical readings. Verse references, quotation boundaries and terminal punctuation vary by textual witness; they need not be identical in the daily printed edition.

notes.en: This witness says “lacks bread, lacks faith”; the daily witness shortens this to “lacks bread, faith.” In the second quotation from Va'yeekruh, this text has “their God,” against “your God” in the daily witness: “their” and “your” are distinct forms. The ending here also includes “and so forth” after “He will give strength to His king.”

notes.en: “Evil inclination” is split between two source paragraphs but is a single expression. In the opening, Ya'akoav's words about honoring Father are understood contextually as referring to Aisuv in his father's presence. The hair-arranging image repeats “his hair and on his head”; it does not introduce another person. In the second interpretation, the future servant is Aisuv and the ruler is Ya'akoav.

דבר אחר: "טוב נקלה (ועבד לו)" -- דא יעקב, דמאיך רוחיה לגביה דעשו, בגין דלבתר ליהוי עבד לו וישלוט עלוי, ויתקיים ביה (בראשית כז כט) יעבדוך עמים וישתחוו לך לאומים וגו', ועדיין לא הוה זמניה כלל, אלא בגין דסליק ליה יעקב לבתר יומיא, ועל דא הוה מיד נקלה, ולבתר ההוא דאיהו מתכבד יהא עבד לו, ההוא דאיהו חסר לחם, יהא עבדא לההוא דיהבו ליה רוב דגן ותירוש. 


תא חזי, על דא בגין דידע יעקב דאצטריך ליה השתא אתהפך ליה נקלה, ויותר חכמה ועקימו עבד בדא, מכל מה דעבד לגביה דעשו, דאילו הוה ידע עשו חכמה דא, יקטיל ליה לגרמיה ולא ייתי לדא, אבל כלא עבד בחכמתא, ועליה אמרה חנה (שמואל א ב י) יהו"ה יחתו מריביו וגו', ויתן עז למלכו וגו':
units.english:
“Ya'akoav sent angels.” Rabbi Abbuh said: Why did he stir himself to approach Aisuv? It would have been better for him to remain silent toward him! Rather, Ya'akoav said: “I know that Aisuv is concerned for Father's honor, and he never gives vent to anger in his presence. I know that as long as Father is alive, I am not afraid of him. But now, while Father is alive, I want to be reconciled with him.” Immediately, “Ya'akoav sent angels before him.”

“Ya'akoav sent angels.” Rabbi Shimon opened and said: “Better one lightly esteemed who has a servant than one who honors himself but lacks bread” (Mishlay 12:9). This verse was said concerning the evil inclination, because it is constantly an accuser against human beings. The evil inclination raises a person's heart and will in pride, and he follows after it, arranging his hair and [the hair] on his head, until it grows overbearing toward him and draws him to Gaihinum. But “better one lightly esteemed”: that is the person who does not follow the evil inclination and does not grow proud at all, but lowers his spirit, heart and will before the Holy One, blessed be He. Then that evil inclination becomes his servant: it cannot rule over him, and that person rules over it, as you say, “And you shall rule over it” (Biraishis 4:7). “Than one who honors himself”—as we have said: he honors himself, arranges his hair and grows proud in his spirit. He “lacks bread”: he lacks faith, as you say, “The bread of his God,” and so forth (Va'yeekruh 21:22), and, “The bread of their God they offer,” and so forth (Va'yeekruh 21:6).

Another interpretation: “Better one lightly esteemed (who has a servant)”—this is Ya'akoav, who lowered his spirit before Aisuv so that afterward [Aisuv] would be his servant and he would rule over him, and there would be fulfilled in him: “Peoples shall serve you, and nations bow down to you,” and so forth (Biraishis 27:29). His time had not yet come at all; rather, Ya'akoav deferred it to the end of days. Therefore he was, for the present, lightly esteemed; afterward, the one who honors himself would be his servant. The one who lacks bread would be a servant to the one to whom an abundance of grain and new wine had been given.

Come and see: therefore, because Ya'akoav knew that he needed this now, he made himself lightly esteemed before him. In this he acted with more wisdom and cunning than in everything he had done toward Aisuv. Had Aisuv known this wisdom, he would have killed himself rather than come to this. But he [Ya'akoav] did everything with wisdom. Of him Channuh said: “Hashem—His adversaries shall be shattered,” and so forth, “and He will give strength to His king,” and so forth (I Samuel 2:10).

introduction.he: הקטע שואל מדוע יעקב יזם פנייה לעשו, ומעמיד את עניין כבוד אביהם כרקע לבקשת הפיוס. אחר כך נדרשת ההשוואה שבמשלי בין מי שנראה נקלה ויש לו עבד ובין מתכבד החסר לחם: תחילה ביחס ליצר הרע, ואחר כך ביחס להכנעת יעקב לפני עשו ולמועד העתידי של הברכה.
introduction.en: The passage asks why Ya'akoav initiated contact with Aisuv, placing concern for their father's honor in the background of his wish for reconciliation. It then expounds Mishlay's contrast between a lightly esteemed person who has a servant and a self-important person who lacks bread: first concerning the evil inclination, then concerning Ya'akoav's lowering himself before Aisuv and the future time of the blessing.

explanation.he: הדרשה הופכת את מראית הכבוד: גאווה מעמידה את האדם תחת שלטון היצר, ואילו שפלות לפני הקב״ה מאפשרת לו למשול בו. ״לחם״ נדרש כאמונה, בלי לבטל את דימוי המחסור שבפסוק. אצל יעקב, ההכנעה בהווה אינה מתוארת כוויתור על הברכה, אלא כדחיית הופעת שלטונו לזמנו. דברי הקטע על תגובתו האפשרית של עשו הם תיאור חריף של עומק התחבולה, לא עצה לפגיעה עצמית ולא כלל להתנהגות כלפי הזולת.
explanation.en: The exposition reverses the appearance of honor: pride places a person under the inclination's rule, while humility before the Holy One, blessed be He, enables him to rule over it. “Bread” is interpreted as faith without removing the verse's image of deprivation. In Ya'akoav's case, present submission is not described as surrender of the blessing, but as postponement of the manifestation of his rule until its time. The passage's words about Aisuv's possible response are a forceful description of the depth of the stratagem, not advice for self-harm or a general rule for conduct toward others.
